title: Connection warmup hedge and soft-deny window to reduce failure cascades
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: We observed a pattern during regional failovers where a large fraction of short-lived connections rejoined immediately after a brief outage which caused a cascading spike in payloads, rehydration KV loads, and tokenized work that briefly violated per-tenant SLO windows. This PR introduces a connection warmup hedge and a soft-deny window to smooth rejoin traffic and give the serving pool time to restore caches and prefix/KV warm state.

What this changes: Adds a tenant-aware connection warmup state machine that tags reconnections with a low-priority warmup flag for a configurable window (default 8s). During warmup, requests are subject to a soft-deny gate: lightweight requests (probes, health pings) are allowed, but heavy requests that trigger KV-prefetch or large-batch execution are rate-limited and demoted into a background warm queue. We also add an adaptive warmup multiplier that reduces the warm window if the region shows stable health signals.

Design notes: warmup decisions are made at the regional connection proxy and propagated in a short-lived header (x-rw-warmup: {flag, window, priority}). The runtime respects that header when deciding to inline or enqueue. To prevent tenant starvation we cap the per-tenant warm queue to a soft fraction of the node (configurable). Telemetry includes new histograms for warmup-duration, warm-queue-latency, rejoin-spike-rate, and per-tenant warm-drop-rate.

Safety and rollback: Feature is behind a runtime flag and an operator toggle in the Console. Default rollout is off; this PR enables the flag in the staging cluster for soak tests. If we observe higher than expected client errors or SLO regressions we revert by flipping the flag or cherry-picking the revert commit.

Checklist: [x] unit tests for state machine transitions; [x] integration test for soft-deny behavior under simulated rejoin storm; [x] telemetry dashboards and alert queries; [x] Console toggle + docs; [x] migration note for older proxies that ignore the header (they will treat it as no-warmup).

Related: ENG-9876 (regional failover smoothing), SUP-4123 (customer report of cascading rejoin), ENG-9901 (warm cache telemetry).
